import pytest
from target import prime_fib


# Equivalence class: n=1, first Fibonacci-prime in the sequence (docstring-confirmed)
def test_n1_first_prime_fib():
    assert prime_fib(1) == 2


# Equivalence class: n=2, second Fibonacci-prime (docstring-confirmed)
def test_n2_second_prime_fib():
    assert prime_fib(2) == 3


# Equivalence class: n=3, third Fibonacci-prime (docstring-confirmed)
def test_n3_third_prime_fib():
    assert prime_fib(3) == 5


# Boundary: mid-range index into the Fibonacci sequence (docstring-confirmed)
def test_n4_fourth_prime_fib():
    assert prime_fib(4) == 13


# Boundary: deeper index into the Fibonacci sequence (docstring-confirmed)
def test_n5_fifth_prime_fib():
    assert prime_fib(5) == 89


# Equivalence class: extends beyond docstring examples; primality of 233 verified
# via SMT (no divisor d in [2,232] with 233 % d == 0)
def test_n6_sixth_prime_fib():
    assert prime_fib(6) == 233


# Equivalence class: larger n requiring deeper sequence traversal; primality of
# 1597 verified via SMT (no divisor d in [2,1596] with 1597 % d == 0)
def test_n7_seventh_prime_fib():
    assert prime_fib(7) == 1597


# Counterexample/boundary: n=0 makes the while-loop condition `c_prime < n`
# false from the start (c_prime starts at 0). SMT proved the loop-invariant
# n<=0 => Not(c_prime < n), so the loop body never executes and the initial
# b=1 is returned instead of raising or looping indefinitely.
def test_n_zero_returns_initial_b():
    assert prime_fib(0) == 1


# Counterexample/boundary: negative n triggers the same loop-invariant as n=0
# (SMT-proved: n<=0 implies loop body never executes), so the function
# returns the initial b=1 rather than erroring on a negative index.
def test_n_negative_returns_initial_b():
    assert prime_fib(-5) == 1
